text:
alex: Quick thread — we saw an incident where a canary rollback failed to recover latency because the fallback variant's KV cache was cold after a traffic surge. Thinking about snapshot-based warmups + surge protection. Any thoughts?

maya: Ah yeah. Spike + instant cutover -> fallback cold start. Did we lose prefix cache or just KV? :thinking:

jon: Mostly KV cache (decoder keys). Prefix cache persisted but KV is per-GPU session. After rollback we ended up reprovisioning many small pods and missed warmup window.

priya: Two ideas: 1) snapshot & restore KV to new variant during handoff; 2) traffic-surge gate that staggers cutover based on available warm capacity.

alex: Snapshot/restore seems promising but we need a fast, consistent format and an atomicity guarantee. Also security (no PII) but it's model state only.

jon: Implementation sketch:
```yaml
fallback:
  snapshot_interval_ms: 5000
  max_snapshot_size_mb: 32
  restore_timeout_ms: 3000
  checksum: true
```
Pushing snapshots to shared fast store (local NVMe + ephemeral S3) then streaming into new router.

maya: Concern: snapshot size and restore time vary with sequence length. Could block cutover and increase latency.

priya: Mitigation: hybrid approach — "hot handoff" for top-k hot prefixes + background restore for full KV. That way small latency hit only.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary 2026-06-07T09:45Z -> cut 20% traffic to variant B. Observability hooks added: kv_snapshot_count, restore_latency_ms.

alex: Also need policy for degraded restores — if restore fails, fallback to partial restore + redirect some traffic to primary or a lower-capacity pool. We don't want cascading failures.

jon: Proposal for circuit:
- pre-cutover check: available warm workers >= X
- snapshot push success >= Y
- on-cutover: allow progressive ramp with surge protection tokens
- on failed restore: auto-rollback + alert

maya: Think about security & audit: snapshots should be encrypted with tenant key and immediately expired after restore.

priya: Ops UX: add toggle in console: "fast-snapshot-warmup: on | off" with metrics expected. Also a playbook section.

alex: TL;DR: build snapshot API + small gating logic + progressive ramp. Owners: eng-runtime for snapshot, eng-infra for store/crypto, eng-platform for gating + console. Can we get volunteers to draft an RFC?

jon: I can take runtime sketch. @maya you good on infra storage & kms? @priya platform gating?

maya: Yep. I'll draft storage/KMS constraints.

priya: Yep, will draft gating + console work and a simple UX flow.

alex: Great. I'll create RFC stub and ping infra + runtime. Thanks everyone :tada:
